name: Class III All-Terrain Vehicle
description: A motorcycle that travels on two tires while it's being ridden off the highway, which is how Oregon classes an electric dirt bike on trails and riding areas.

restrictions.rule: A two-wheeled motorcycle being ridden off the highway; no limit on motor power or speed (Oregon Revised Statutes §801.194)
Needs an ATV operating permit and decal from Oregon Parks and Recreation, valid for two years, to ride where the land manager requires one (Oregon Revised Statutes §821.195)
Riders 16 or older need an ATV safety education card on public lands (Oregon Revised Statutes §821.172)
Riders under 16 need the card and a hands-on course, and must be accompanied by someone 18 or older who holds an ATV card (Oregon Revised Statutes §821.172)
Riders under 7 may not ride on public lands (Oregon Revised Statutes §821.172)
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a DOT motorcycle helmet with the chin strap fastened (Oregon Revised Statutes §821.202)
Kept off highways, their shoulders and medians, except to cross, load or unload, or where posted open to all-terrain vehicles (Oregon Revised Statutes §§821.190, 821.200)
No insurance needed off the highway
